data.title: Maisons du Monde tightens costs and cleans up balance sheet as sales slide
data.description:
An announcement from Maisons du Monde SA ( (FR:MDM) ) is now available.

Maisons du Monde reported first‑half 2026 net sales of €412.8 million, down 7.1% year‑on‑year amid a sluggish home furnishings market and constrained inventory levels, with sharper declines in online activity and weaker performance in Germany and Austria. Despite a deeper current EBIT loss of €36.8 million and a gross margin contraction, the group delivered €15 million in cost savings, improved working capital through inventory reductions, and narrowed its net loss to €64 million.

Free cash flow remained negative at €49.8 million but improved versus 2025, while operating costs fell 4.8% thanks to logistics and transport efficiencies, partly offset by inflation and IT‑related transformation costs. Following a comprehensive refinancing completed in July, pro forma net financial debt was cut to €24.6 million, leaving the company with a cleaned‑up balance sheet and greater financial stability to pursue its turnaround and long‑term profitability objectives under the backing of new shareholders.

data.title: Moleculin Highlights Immune-Driven Annamycin Pancreatic Cancer Data
data.description:
Moleculin Biotech ( (MBRX) ) has provided an update.

On September 25, 2026, Moleculin Biotech reported new preclinical data showing that its lead drug Annamycin (naxtarubicin) exerts antitumor activity in pancreatic cancer partly through CD8+ T cell cytotoxicity. The data, presented at the AACR Conference on Pancreatic Cancer in San Diego, suggest Annamycin may help convert immunologically “cold” pancreatic tumors into “hot” tumors that are more susceptible to immune attack.

Because pancreatic cancer’s cold immune microenvironment has limited the effectiveness of checkpoint inhibitors, the evidence of an immune-mediated component to Annamycin’s activity highlights potential for future combination strategies and scientific alignment with Moleculin’s immune-modulating WP1066 program. The findings remain confined to preclinical models and are not part of the ongoing MIRACLE trial in acute myeloid leukemia, so they do not immediately alter Moleculin’s clinical focus but could broaden the long-term therapeutic scope of Annamycin if similar effects are demonstrated in humans.

data.title: Accsys Investors Approve All AGM Resolutions and Switch Auditor to Deloitte
data.description:
Accsys Technologies ( (GB:AXS) ) has shared an announcement.

Accsys Technologies PLC said shareholders approved all resolutions at its annual general meeting on 25 September 2026, underscoring broad investor support for the specialist wood materials group. Ordinary resolutions included receipt of the 2026 financial statements, endorsement of the directors’ remuneration report, reappointment of all serving directors and authorisation for the board to allot shares, with voting participation representing about 41.7% of the issued share capital.

Investors also backed several key special resolutions, granting directors authority to disapply pre-emption rights over up to roughly 20% of the company’s share capital, permitting market purchases of Accsys shares and allowing general meetings to be called on 14 days’ notice. Deloitte LLP was appointed as the new auditor following a competitive tender, after PwC stepped down due to the length of its tenure; PwC confirmed it had no issues to flag, signalling a smooth transition in oversight that supports Accsys’s governance and future financing flexibility.

data.title: Regeneron Steps Into Obesity Drug Race With New Phase 1 Study
data.description:
Regeneron Pharmaceuticals (REGN) announced an update on their ongoing clinical study.

Regeneron Pharmaceuticals, Inc. (REGN) is running a Phase 1 study called “A Phase 1, Randomized, Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled Study of the Safety, Tolerability, and Pharmacokinetics of Single Ascending Doses of REGN20934 in Adult Participants With Overweight or Obesity.” The goal is to check safety and early drug behavior in the body, laying groundwork for Regeneron’s push into the fast-growing obesity treatment market.

The study tests REGN20934, an injectable drug candidate aimed at adults with overweight or obesity. It is designed to help manage weight over time if later trials confirm benefits, positioning Regeneron as a potential new player alongside established obesity drug leaders.

The study was first submitted on May 11, 2026, marking the formal start of the clinical path for this asset. The listing was last updated on September 23, 2026, showing that the protocol details and recruitment status are current and that the program is actively managed.

For investors, this early-stage obesity study adds optionality to REGN’s pipeline at a time when demand for weight-loss drugs is reshaping pharma valuations. Success would support a longer-term growth story and help Regeneron compete with leaders like Novo Nordisk and Eli Lilly, though near-term stock impact will likely be modest until later-phase efficacy data emerge.
